budget_items.what_was_said: The proposed FY27 omnibus balanced budget was read into the record along with the transfers that fund it from several enterprise and revolving funds; the committee later split 4-1-1 on recommending it.

budget_items.topic: Fire department fourth shift and added staffing
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the fire chief's budget added a person to every shift beyond the fourth-shift addition itself, and that this was hard to get a straight answer on in the chief's presentation.

budget_items.topic: Assistant town manager and HR director positions
budget_items.what_was_said: A member argued these two new/changed positions have no job description or scope and objected to their combined cost while other services are being cut.

budget_items.topic: Article M — Proposition 2½ override, tier one and tier two
budget_items.what_was_said: The article proposes a tier one and a tier two override; a member argued residents were never offered a true level-services option and called the structure coercive.

budget_items.topic: Tax impact table for the override tiers
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair walked through a table showing the tax rate and bill impact of the balanced budget, tier one, and tier two on homes from $250,000 to $1.55 million, using the median assessed home value as an example.
The committee reviewed and recommended the cable/PEG access enterprise budget, noting it draws down retained earnings and faces longer-term revenue pressure from cord-cutting.

budget_items.topic: Article EE — adding two positions to the salary grid
budget_items.what_was_said: Placing the assistant town manager and HR director positions on the salary grid has financial implications depending on the grade assigned; a member said this should have followed the town's normal job-description process.
The committee revoted a prior 4-1 appropriation for the anniversary committee so the chair's vote could be included.

budget_items.topic: Article Q2 — special purpose (health insurance) stabilization fund
budget_items.what_was_said: A member objected that no parameters were set for when the reserve could be tapped and called free cash a slush fund; others said any withdrawal still requires town meeting approval.
A member noted the recycling line appeared reduced only because it moved to actuals, and asked for continued tracking of ways to make the program more affordable.

decisions.decision: Ask the town manager/Jen to add a reference in the warrant summaries for articles L and M pointing readers to the finance committee's annual report.
Create a tracking list/spreadsheet of items the committee has asked departments to look into, reviewed roughly quarterly.
Start budget discussions with departments earlier, in the fall, similar to this year's tri-board process, before departments finalize their budget requests.
Continue the practice of submitting questions to departments in writing in advance rather than asking live during meetings.
Hold a retrospective meeting in May after town meeting to prepare the incoming committee given expected turnover in June.
Schedule the next Finance Committee meeting for April 23; no meeting will be held April 9.

minutes.summary: The Finance Committee re-voted a batch of previously split or 5-member warrant-article recommendations so the chair's vote could be added, and worked through remaining deferred articles for the May town meeting warrant, most consequentially the FY27 omnibus balanced budget and the two-tier Proposition 2½ override. One member repeatedly argued the balanced budget under-documents new positions (an assistant town manager and HR director) and cuts services in a way designed to pressure voters toward the override, while other members defended the process and voted to recommend both override tiers. The committee also approved its FY27 annual report for inclusion in the mailed warrant and set its next meeting for April 23.

what_happened.line: Finance Committee voted 4-2 to recommend both tiers of a Proposition 2½ override for town meeting.
The FY27 omnibus balanced budget was recommended on a split 4-1-1 vote after a member argued it under-documents two new positions.
The committee voted 4-2 to add the assistant town manager and HR director positions to the salary grid, which a member said bypassed the town's normal job-description process.
Several prior 5-0 and other warrant-article recommendations were re-voted so the chair's vote could be added before the warrant is finalized.
The next Finance Committee meeting was set for April 23, skipping April 9.

why_it_matters: Town meeting will vote on both override tiers as well as the underlying FY27 budget, so a resident's tax bill depends on which of these articles pass.
Adding the two new town-hall positions to the salary grid affects what those roles cost the town, and the committee's recommendation was split, not unanimous.
The re-votes and the finance committee's own annual report will accompany the warrant residents receive by mail before they vote.
watch_next: May town meeting, where article L (FY27 budget) and article M (the two override tiers) go to a town-wide vote

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on which articles passed and by what roll-call margin — every override, EE, GG, L, X, and the no-financial-impact vote match — but the official minutes carry almost none of the dollar figures, transfer amounts, or tax-impact numbers that ours captured, and the two records give flatly different subject matter for "Article Q." The one thing a reader should check first is Article Q: ours says it's the 300th-anniversary committee appropriation ($15,000), the official minutes say it's the General Purpose Stabilization Fund Transfer — both records agree the vote was 5-1, but not on what was voted for.
